problem: Given $P(A)=0.25$, $P(B)=0.75$, $P(A\cup B)=0.8$, determine whether  $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.

choices.value: $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events, since $P(A\cap B)=0$
$A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events, since $P(A)\cdot P(B)\ne P(A\cup B)$
$A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events, since $P(A\cap B)\ne 0$
$A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events, since $P(A)\cdot P(B)<P(A\cup B)$
$A$ and $B$ are not mutually exclusive events, since $P(A)\ne P(B)$

examples.knowledge_point: Determining Whether Two Events are Mutually Exclusive
examples.problem: Given $P(A)=\dfrac{1}{3},$ $P(B)=\dfrac{1}{4},$ and $P(A\cup B)=\dfrac{7}{12},$ determine whether $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.
examples.worked_solution:
To check if $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, we must check that $P(A\cap B) = 0.$

We can calculate $P(A\cap B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{7}{12} & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}-P(A\cap B) \\ P(A\cap B) & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}-\frac{7}{12} \\  & =\frac{4+3-7}{12} \\  & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.
